value.body: Medical Officers in a state health service run primary health centres, community health centres and district hospitals — treating patients, running national health programmes and managing staff. It is the main government career for MBBS doctors, with promotions up to senior administrative posts in the state health directorate.

items.label: Qualification
items.note: Some states add a local-language requirement

items.label: Recruiting body
items.value: State PSC or state health recruitment board
items.note: Varies by state; National Health Mission also hires MOs on contract

items.label: Central alternative
items.note: For central government health services and railways

value.title: How you get in
value.body: MBBS with internship and registration with the state medical council or NMC. States recruit through their Public Service Commission or a dedicated medical / health recruitment board, through a written test, interview or merit list depending on the state.

value.title: At a glance
items: Early postings are often in rural or remote centres.
Many states have service bonds for government-college graduates; bond terms and penalties differ by state.
Several states offer in-service quotas or incentive marks for NEET-PG to doctors with rural service.
Promotion titles differ by state (e.g. Senior MO, Civil Surgeon, CMO, Deputy / Joint Director).
